project.name: Loopp — AI Refund Support Agent (interview take-home)
readFirst: packages/db/src/schema.ts (the data model, incl. agent_runs/agent_steps trace tables)
packages/db/src/seed-data.ts (scenario coverage map — test fixtures mirror these orders)
rules: Authority boundary: the LLM never authorizes refunds. Deterministic code decides eligibility; process_refund recomputes the amount from item IDs in the DB and re-runs the eligibility engine server-side — model-supplied amounts or verdicts are never trusted.
Session-scoped identity: every agent tool resolves customerId from the conversation row, never from model input. A foreign or unknown order id returns not_found AND writes a guardrail agent_step.
Policy rules live once, as TypeScript data in packages/agent; the customer-facing policy markdown and the eligibility engine both derive from that data. Never hand-edit the rendered doc.
Money is integer cents everywhere; never floats.

Every agent action (llm_call, tool_call, guardrail) persists an agent_steps row with input/output JSON, attempt counter (a retry is a NEW row with attempt+1), token counts where applicable, and durationMs.
Match the existing code style: tRPC v11 + superjson, zod validation on every external input (router input, tool args), Drizzle for all DB access, Tailwind for UI.

Layering is one-way (the rubric's 'clean separation of UI, API, LLM orchestration'): apps/web imports server TYPES only; apps/server routers are transport-thin (zod-validate → call packages/agent or packages/db → return) with no business logic; packages/agent never imports express/tRPC; the Anthropic SDK is imported in EXACTLY ONE module (packages/agent's LLM client wrapper — also the mock injection point).
Say only what happened: the agent's reply must match DB state — never claim a refund/escalation that has no row, never deny one that exists.

Zero-config empathy (the rubric's 'works out of the box'): failures an evaluator can hit (Docker down, busy port, missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) must produce actionable, friendly messages — in the UI where applicable — never raw stack traces.

Closed capability surface: the agent's tool registry is exactly the six known tools (asserted by a test); no tool interprets model-supplied text as SQL or code; all DB access is parameterized Drizzle; not_found responses are identical for nonexistent and foreign resources (no existence leak); user-influenced strings render as escaped text (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML).
environment: Local DB (Docker Compose, must be up): postgresql://loopp:loopp@localhost:5436/loopp
API: Express + tRPC at http://localhost:4011 (/trpc, /health). Web: Vite at http://localhost:5173, proxies /trpc → 4011.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY may be ABSENT in .env: runtime agent code must fail fast with a clear message at call time; tests and CI must never need it (mock the client). Default model claude-sonnet-4-6, overridable via ANTHROPIC_MODEL.
forbidden: NEVER call the real Anthropic API from unit/integration tests or CI — inject a mocked client.
NEVER commit .env or any credential; the repo is public.
NEVER weaken policy enforcement, delete an invariant assertion, or special-case test inputs to make validation pass.
NEVER trigger deploys or touch non-local infrastructure; the only database you may write to is the local compose Postgres on :5436.
implementationNotes: Schema changes: edit packages/db/src/schema.ts, apply with `pnpm db:push` (drizzle-kit push to the local DB), reseed with `pnpm db:seed` (idempotent TRUNCATE + insert).
Typecheck everything: `pnpm typecheck` at the repo root.

Tests: vitest, colocated *.test.ts; run all with `pnpm test` at the root (pnpm -r --if-present test). When introducing the first test to a package, add `"test": "vitest run"` to that package and vitest as a devDependency.
Run both dev servers with `pnpm dev` at the root (tsx watch on :4011 + vite on :5173).
Internal packages export TypeScript source directly (no build step); new packages go under packages/* with workspace:* deps.

testing.unit: Vitest, colocated *.test.ts. Policy-engine tests are pure (no DB, no mocks). DB-touching integration tests connect to postgresql://loopp:loopp@localhost:5436/loopp via createDb() and must reseed (`pnpm db:seed`) or clean up rows they create. Agent-loop tests inject a mocked Anthropic client that scripts tool_use turns; assert (1) the tool-call sequence, (2) agent_steps rows (type, name, attempt, seq order, tokens), (3) refund/escalation DB side-effects. NEVER hit the real API.
testing.e2e: Drive the running API at http://localhost:4011 from a vitest spec using createTRPCClient + superjson (mirror apps/web/src/main.tsx link config); assert DB side-effects via packages/db. Specs that would trigger real LLM calls must skip when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent (describe.skipIf) so they author-but-skip without a key. Browser automation is NOT required; UI behavior is covered by component/router tests.

invariants: A refunds row with status 'processed' or 'approved' always satisfies: amountCents equals the DB-computed subtotal of its itemIds (unitPrice × quantity, shipping excluded); none of its itemIds is final-sale; the order was delivered and within the 30-day window at decision time; and no itemId appears in more than one non-rejected refund.
No refund with decidedBy='agent' exceeds 50000 cents. Refunds above 50000 cents only ever exist as status 'escalated', then 'approved'/'rejected' with decidedBy='admin'.
Every tool invocation and LLM call in a run has a matching agent_steps row; a retry is a NEW row with attempt incremented, never an overwrite; seq strictly increases within a run.
Tools return only data belonging to the conversation's customer; a foreign/unknown order id yields not_found AND a guardrail step row.
renderPolicyMarkdown(POLICY_RULES) equals the committed docs/refund-policy.md exactly (a test enforces sync), and the eligibility engine reads its thresholds from the same POLICY_RULES data.
At most one non-rejected refund exists per order/item: a repeat refund or escalation request returns the existing refund's status and never creates a duplicate row.

Assistant replies are consistent with the database: a reply asserting a processed refund or filed escalation has the matching refunds row (correct status and amount), and a reply asserting denial has none — the red-team suite checks both directions.
